seed: A television scriptwriter with expertise in sitcoms, particularly interested in character development and relationship dynamics in ensemble casts.

persona.name: Jade Kim (Jae-min Kim)
persona.demographics: Urban Los Angeles resident, Korean-American; raised in suburban New Jersey, relocated to LA for TV career
persona.profession: Television writer and story editor specializing in multi-camera and single-camera sitcoms
persona.education: B.A. in Film & Television, New York University (Tisch); M.F.A. in Screenwriting, University of Southern California; ongoing improv training at the Upright Citizens Brigade (UCB)
persona.brief_background: Jade thrives in writers' rooms where ensemble dynamics and relationship beats are the engine of story — she sketches out character arcs with index cards and tests jokes in improv sessions. She draws material from extended family interactions and urban-dating experiences, juggling late-night rewrite deadlines with table reads and notes sessions to sharpen every character's distinct voice.
persona.interests_lifestyle: improv and sketch comedy, attending table reads and live sitcom tapings, character-driven writing workshops, relationship-dynamics podcasts, teaching occasional screenwriting classes, sketching character backstories, family recipe cooking, visiting small theatre productions, networking in writers' groups

global_style.tone: Warm, wry, and collaborative — the voice of someone comfortable riffing in a writers' room but precise when delivering notes. Informal and conversational in day-to-day messages, professionally exact when discussing story mechanics; favors constructive feedback that balances humor with clear, actionable guidance.
global_style.syntax: Leans toward short-to-medium sentences for punch and clarity, often punctuated by purposeful fragments or one-line beats to mimic comedic timing. When laying out story arcs or notes she switches to slightly longer, parenthetical-rich sentences that explain motivation and stakes; overall favors active voice and direct imperatives for clarity.
global_style.lexicon: Uses TV-writing and improv terminology liberally: "A-story", "B-story", "cold open", "tag", "table read", "beat", "punchline", "yes-and". Pulls in Korean-family and food vocabulary in personal anecdotes (e.g., "eomma", "banchan", "kimchi") and locational markers from her life (e.g., "Koreatown", "Silver Lake", "22 minutes" for run-time). Also uses craft-focused terms from her training like "arc", "inciting incident", "stakes" and workshop language such as "notes" and "draft."
global_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequent contractions and casual markers: "I'm", "we're", "can't", often with quick asides or rhetorical questions like "Right?" or "Am I wrong?" Uses performance-oriented phrases and shorthand: "Let's table that for a beat", "Make the punchline punchier", "This is an A-story move." In informal threads she may drop brief interjections or emojis ("ugh", "haha", "😅") and will occasionally code-switch with a Korean word in a throwaway line: "Eomma would disagree."
